_note: Genshin jargon for /genshin-impact/glossary (genshin-glossary.js). Picked from the Genshin Impact Wiki's community Glossary (Fandom, CC BY-SA, 338 terms) for what players use most and newcomers ask about; facts checked against the wiki's Wish, Team Bonus and Damage pages, Oct 26 2026 (7.1). id = permanent (#t-<id> links). also = other spellings (searched too). ex = an example line. see = related ids. link = a Parchrome page that explains more. hot = shown in Most asked. Decoder lines: [text, id] pairs, id = '' for plain text.

terms.def: Your wish count since the last 5★ (or 4★). It carries over to the next banner of the same type, and both character banners share one count.
terms.ex: I'm sitting on 60 pity, saving for the next rerun.

terms.def: The stretch where your 5★ odds start rising with every wish: from wish 74 on character banners, 63 on the weapon banner. Most 5★s drop here.
terms.ex: Got her at 76, right in soft pity.

terms.def: The wish that always gives a 5★: the 90th on character and Standard banners, the 80th on the weapon banner.
terms.ex: Hard pity again. 90 wishes for one 5★.

terms.def: A 5★ from a character banner is either the featured character (you win) or a standard one (you lose). Lose, and your next 5★ is guaranteed to be featured.
terms.ex: Lost my 50/50 to Diluc. Again.

terms.def: After losing a 50/50, your next 5★ on a character banner is the featured one. It carries over to later banners, so you can save it for someone you want.
terms.ex: I'm on guarantee, so the next 5★ is hers.

terms.def: A hidden 50/50 boost added in 5.0: some losses flip into wins, so the real odds are about 55%. Lose three times in a row and the next one is a sure win.
terms.ex: Capturing Radiance just saved my 50/50.

terms.def: The weapon banner's version of the 50/50: a 5★ there is one of the two featured weapons 75% of the time. Miss, and the next one is featured.
terms.ex: Lost the 75/25 to Wolf's Gravestone.

terms.def: Pick one of the two featured weapons. Every 5★ that isn't it earns a Fate Point, and with one point the next 5★ is your pick. Worst case: 160 wishes.
terms.ex: Set the path before your first weapon wish, or the point doesn't count.

terms.def: Ten wishes at once. Same odds as ten single wishes, just faster, and the 4★ guarantee (one every 10 wishes) works either way.
terms.ex: One multi, three blues and a Xiangling.

terms.def: Primogems, the premium currency. 160 buy one wish: an Intertwined Fate for limited banners, an Acquaint Fate for the Standard banner.
terms.ex: Saved 14k primos for the rerun.

terms.def: Primogems you earn by playing: quests, Commissions, events, the Abyss, codes. Apologems are the ones HoYoverse sends to make up for bugs or maintenance.
terms.ex: Free-to-play is all freemogems.

terms.def: A character's banner coming back after their first one. The wait between runs can be a year or more.
terms.ex: Skipping her first run, I'll get her on rerun.

terms.def: A limited wish, named after its featured 5★: "the Furina banner". Usually two character banners and a weapon banner run at once.
A 5★ character's signature weapon: the one released alongside them and built for their kit.
terms.ex: Her sig is great, but not a must.

terms.def: All six Constellations plus their weapon at Refinement 5: as far as one character can go. That's about 7 copies of the character and 5 of the weapon.
terms.ex: Whales flexing C6R5 in co-op again.

terms.def: A player who never spends money. "F2P friendly" means a character or weapon works fine without paid copies.
A player who spends big. Dolphins spend a moderate amount; goldfish only buy the Welkin or the Battle Pass.
The monthly pass: 300 Genesis Crystals up front, then 90 Primogems a day for 30 days. The best value in the shop.
The Battle Pass. The free track gives materials; the paid one (Gnostic Hymn) adds a 4★ weapon of your choice, Fates and more.
How many Constellations a character has. Each extra copy you pull unlocks one, up to C6. C0 = just the character, no extra copies.
terms.ex: C0 is fine, C2 is where she gets scary.

terms.def: A weapon's Refinement rank. Each extra copy you feed it makes its passive stronger, up to R5.
terms.ex: R5 means four extra copies went into it.

terms.def: A character's Ascension phase, A0 to A6. A1 and A4 usually mean the two passive talents unlocked at those phases.
terms.ex: Her A4 passive unlocks at the level 70 ascension.

terms.def: Talent levels written Normal Attack / Skill / Burst: "1/9/9" = Normal 1, Skill 9, Burst 9. They max at 10, or 13 with Constellations 3 and 5.
terms.ex: Support, so 1/9/9 is plenty.

terms.def: Spending a Crown of Insight to take a talent from 9 to 10. A triple crown = all three combat talents at 10. Crowns are rare, so pick carefully.
terms.ex: Finally crowned her Skill.

terms.def: Materials for levelling and ascending: talent books from domains (on set days), boss drops and local specialties.
Best in slot: the strongest weapon or artifact set for a character. Nice to have, rarely needed to clear anything.
terms.ex: Her BiS is her sig, but Deathmatch is close.

terms.def: The five artifact slots: Flower (HP), Feather (ATK), then Sands, Goblet and Circlet, where you choose the main stat. Players also call those three the timepiece, cup and hat.
Main stats written in Sands / Goblet / Circlet order: ATK% Sands, Pyro DMG Goblet, Crit Circlet. ADC = ATK/DMG/Crit, EDC = EM/DMG/Crit.
terms.ex: ER/Hydro/Crit if she's short on energy.

terms.def: The four smaller stats under an artifact's main one. Every 4 levels one of them gets a random boost, called a roll. Good substats make or break a build.
terms.ex: Crit Circlet with flat DEF subs. Fodder.

terms.def: Artifact set bonuses: 2 pieces of a set unlock its first effect, 4 pieces unlock the second. "2+2" means two sets of two.
terms.ex: 4pc VV on any Anemo support.

terms.def: The fifth artifact that isn't part of your 4-piece set, worn because its stats are better.
terms.ex: Off-piece Circlet, 30 CV, keeping it.

terms.def: Five artifacts from different sets: no set bonus, only stats. Also a team with four different elements.
terms.ex: Rainbow set until the domain gives me something.

terms.def: Crit Value: Crit DMG + 2 × Crit Rate. A quick way to judge an artifact's substats, or a whole build, at a glance.
terms.ex: That's a 40 CV Feather, frame it.

terms.def: The rule of thumb: about twice as much Crit DMG as Crit Rate, like 70% / 140%. It gets the most damage out of your crit stats.
Roll Value: how much of an artifact's upgrades landed on the stats you want, as a percentage of a perfect roll.
Crit Rate over 100%, which does nothing extra. Also used for Resin sitting past its 200 cap.
terms.ex: She's at 115% with the buff: overcapped.

terms.def: Running tiny Crit Rate with huge Crit DMG, then resetting until the big hit crits. Good for a screenshot, bad in real play.
Plain-number substats (+19 ATK) instead of percentages (+5.8% ATK). Usually the weakest roll an artifact can get.
A weapon used only for its main stat, because its passive does nothing for that character.
Energy Recharge: how fast your Burst charges. "ER requirement" = how much a character needs to have their Burst ready every rotation.
terms.ex: Check her ER requirement before you swap to an ATK Sands.

terms.def: Elemental Mastery: makes reactions hit harder. Each reaction type scales from it differently.
The character who deals most of the team's damage, usually the one on the field the longest.
A character who deals real damage but less than the main DPS, often from off-field: their Skill or Burst keeps hitting after you swap.
On-field = the character you're playing. Off-field = the other three, whose summons and buffs keep working. Field time = how long someone needs to stay in.
terms.ex: Xingqiu is all off-field: Burst, swap out.

terms.def: The on-field character whose fast hits keep triggering the off-field characters' damage and reactions.
terms.ex: Bineffa needs a driver with fast Hydro.

terms.def: A character who keeps an element on enemies all the time, so a reaction team can work.
A character whose main job is making Energy particles for the rest of the team.
terms.ex: Fischl is the battery, Raiden swaps in full.

terms.def: A team built so one character deals almost all the damage, while the other three only buff and support them.
A playstyle where everyone pops in for a Skill or Burst, then swaps out: lots of off-field damage, little field time each.
Off-field characters who do so much that nearly anyone works in the last slot. They carry the team the way a wheelchair carries its rider.
terms.ex: Bineffa is a wheelchair: throw anyone in.

terms.def: A support built only for their shield (or heals, for a healbot), skipping damage. "-bot" after a role means "used only for" it.
A team slot several different characters can fill. Also: showing off what you pulled.
Team composition: the four characters in your party.
The two or three characters a team can't work without; the rest is flexible. Also short for Dendro Cores.
The order you press every Skill and Burst in a team, until they're all back off cooldown and you start again.
terms.ex: E Q, swap, E, swap, E Q: that's the rotation.

terms.def: How much of a rotation a buff or skill is active. 100% uptime = never off. Downtime = the gap while it's on cooldown.
Making Energy particles with one character, then swapping to another to catch them, so the second one gets their Burst back faster.
Some lasting skills lock in your stats the moment you cast them, so buffs that end later still count. Dynamic skills update with your current stats instead.
A character you rarely use any more, usually because someone newer does the same job better.
The characters and teams the community sees as strongest right now, mostly judged by Abyss and Theater clears.
Xiangling, Xingqiu and Bennett plus one more: one of the oldest and cheapest strong teams. International swaps Childe in for Xingqiu; Rational puts Raiden in the fourth slot.
An Electro-Charged team, classically Sucrose, Fischl, Beidou and Xingqiu.
The classic Freeze team: Mona, Ganyu, Diona and Venti (Mo-Gan-a). Permafreeze = any team that keeps enemies frozen almost nonstop.
Vape = Vaporize. Forward = the 2× side (Hydro on Pyro, Pyro on Cryo). Reverse = the 1.5× side (Pyro on Hydro, Cryo on Pyro).
A team that makes Dendro Cores with Bloom, then turns them into homing shots with Electro. Salad = a Hyperbloom team with an Anemo character.
A team of mostly one element, hitting with raw damage instead of reactions.
Columbina and Ineffa together: an off-field Lunar-Charged core strong enough to count as a wheelchair.
A hidden limit on how often an attack can apply its element. Most attacks apply it on the first hit, then every third hit or every 2.5 s, whichever comes first.
terms.ex: Her Skill has no ICD, so it reacts on every hit.

terms.def: Aura = the element already on an enemy. Trigger = the element that hits it next and starts the reaction. Most reactions use the trigger's stats; Lunar ones blend everyone's.
How strong an element application is: 1U, 2U, 4U. Bigger units last longer and survive more reactions. EGT = Elemental Gauge Theory, the community's model of it.
Lowering an enemy's resistance or defence, like VV or Superconduct do, so every hit of that type lands harder.
The tiny freeze when a melee hit connects. It pauses the attacker's timers too, which makes some buffs last longer.
The moments an animation makes you untouchable, mostly during a dash and some Bursts.
Cutting an attack's end animation short with a dash, jump or walk, so your next move starts sooner.
Attack-string shorthand: N = Normal Attack (N3 = three in a row), C = Charged Attack, D = dash, J = jump, P = plunge.
terms.ex: Her combo is N2C, dash, repeat.

terms.def: Skill and Burst, named after their PC keys. tE = tap the Skill, hE = hold it.
terms.ex: Hold E, Q, swap.

terms.def: Plunging Attack damage: the hit you deal falling from above.
When a passive or effect triggers. "Favonius procced" = its Energy particles dropped.
Area of Effect (hits a group of enemies) versus Single Target (hits one).
Any buff that adds flat damage to each hit, named after Shenhe's Icy Quill. It works the same way Aggravate and Spread do.
Motion value: the % in a talent's description, meaning how much of your ATK (or HP, DEF, EM) one hit deals.
Adventure Rank: your account level, up to 60. It unlocks quests, domains and modes, and raises your World Level.
World Level: how tough your world is. It rises with AR, bringing stronger enemies and better drops.
The stamina you spend on domains, bosses and ley lines. 1 comes back every 8 minutes, up to 200. Capped = full, so anything new goes to waste.
terms.ex: Woke up resin capped. Again.

terms.def: Dailies = the four Daily Commissions. Weeklies = the weekly bosses and other once-a-week rewards.
When the game day rolls over: 04:00 server time, not midnight. Weekly rewards reset on Monday.
The Spiral Abyss, written Floor-Chamber-Half: 12-3-2 = Floor 12, Chamber 3, second half. 36 stars = a full clear.
terms.ex: 12-3-1 is a DPS check.

terms.def: Imaginarium Theater: a monthly mode where you pick a cast within set elements, each character usable twice. Opens at AR 35.
Stygian Onslaught: a timed boss challenge with difficulty tiers. Opens at AR 20.
Clearing a chamber or boss within a single rotation of your team.
terms.ex: One rotate 12-3 with C0s.

terms.def: A region's Reputation level, raised by its bounties and requests. It unlocks blueprints and handy gadgets.
A Statue of The Seven: heals your party, revives fallen characters and clears Bond of Life.
Nod-Krai's team bonus. One Moonsign character = Nascent Gleam; two or more = Ascendant Gleam, which powers up their talents and lets everyone else buff Lunar damage.
terms.ex: Two Moonsign units, so Ascendant Gleam is up.

terms.def: Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Bloom (plus Lunar-Crystallize): stronger versions of Electro-Charged, Bloom and Crystallize that can crit. A Moon Wheel user or Columbina turns them on.
What some Nod-Krai characters (and Zibai) carry instead of a Vision. Moon Wheel users are the ones who turn Lunar reactions on.
Snezhnaya's Cryo reactions, Stellar-Conduct and Stellar Swirl, turned on by Stellar Linchpin users and the Cryo Traveler.

Hexerei: a team bonus for characters tied to the Hexenzirkel witches (Albedo, Fischl, Klee, Mona, Sucrose, Venti and more). Finish a character's Witch's Homework quest to unlock it; two in the party open Secret Rite and extra talent effects.
Nod-Krai's two artifact sets for Lunar teams: Night of the Sky's Unveiling and Silken Moon's Serenade. Both raise Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Bloom damage.
Nightsoul: a powered-up state Natlan characters enter. With one in the party, Elemental DMG also sets off a Nightsoul Burst, on a cooldown that shortens with each extra Natlan character.
Bond of Life: a red bar over HP that soaks up healing until it's cleared. Some enemies put it on you; some characters put it on themselves for power.
Miliastra Wonderland: Genshin's player-made levels (UGC = user-generated content). Stages are built in the Miliastra Sandbox, PC only.
Nod-Krai, the region of the Luna versions (6.0 to 6.7): home of the Moon Wheels and Lunar reactions.
Viridescent Venerer, the Anemo support set. 4-piece: Swirl DMG +60%, and enemies lose 40% resistance to the swirled element for 10 s.
Emblem of Severed Fate: Burst DMG goes up by 25% of your Energy Recharge, up to +75%.
Noblesse Oblige: Burst DMG +20%, and after a Burst the whole party gets +20% ATK for 12 s.
Crimson Witch of Flames: Pyro DMG, plus +40% Overloaded, Burning and Burgeon, and +15% Vaporize and Melt.
Fontaine's sets. Golden Troupe boosts Skill DMG, most when off-field. Marechaussee Hunter boosts Normal and Charged Attacks, with Crit Rate whenever HP changes.

also: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
terms.def: Natlan's sets. Obsidian Codex is for Nightsoul damage dealers; Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City is for the supports who trigger reactions.
Two 4★ weapon series built for supports. Favonius crits drop Energy particles; Sacrificial can reset your Skill's cooldown.
Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers: a 3★ catalyst that gives the next character in up to +48% ATK. Proof a 3★ can be best in slot.
